```{r penguins}
data("penguins", package = "palmerpenguins")
summary(penguins)
nrow(penguins)
ncol(penguins)
``` 
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
mean(pull(penguins, flipper_length_mm), na.rm = TRUE)
```
na.rm is a logical evaluating to TRUE or FALSE indicating whether NA values should be stripped before the computation proceeds. Used AI to figure out this argument usage

## Problem 2

 Create a data frame comprised of:


Hint: to take the mean of a variable in a dataframe, you need to pull the variable out of the dataframe. Try loading the tidyverse and using the pull function.

In some cases, you can explicitly convert variables from one type to another. Write a code chunk that applies the as.numeric function to the logical, character, and factor variables (please show this chunk but not the output). What happens, and why? Does this help explain what happens when you try to take the mean?


```{r}

set.seed(1)

problem2_df = tibble(
  vec_numeric= rnorm(10),
  vec_logical= c(vec_numeric>TRUE),
  vec_character= c("It", "is", "cold", "outside", "but", "I", "am", "inside", "right", "now"),
  vec_factor = c("fast", "slow", "fast", "fast", "medium", "fast", "fast", "medium", "slow", "slow")
)

print.data.frame(problem2_df)

library(tidyverse)
mean(pull(problem2_df,vec_numeric))
mean(pull(problem2_df,vec_logical))
mean(pull(problem2_df,vec_character))
mean(pull(problem2_df,vec_factor))

```
I already loaded tidyverse in the first coding section. But put it above again since HW mentioned it

Used print.data.frame since I wanted to see the results.


```{r, results = "hide"}
as.numeric(pull(problem2_df,vec_logical))
as.numeric(pull(problem2_df,vec_character))
as.numeric(pull(problem2_df,vec_factor))
```



EXTRA

* The mean of the sample is `r mean(pull(la_df, norm_samp))`
* The median of the sample is `r median(pull(la_df, norm_samp))`
* The standard deviation of the sample is `r sd(pull(la_df, norm_samp))`

In this dataset, the names of variables include species, island, bill length (mm), bill depth (mm), flipper length (mm), body mass (g), sex, and year

There are 344 rows and 8 columns.
